required_inputs: Frozen public PWR/SB-LOCA manifest with labels, trajectory IDs, counts, units, sampling rate, and horizon (P-NEML-F01-D1-MANIFEST).
Trajectory- and scenario-level train, validation, and held-out identities with zero cross-partition overlap (P-NEML-F01-D1-SPLIT).
Retained records labeled as PWR SB-LOCA transients with declared break-extent unit, sampling rate, and horizon (P-NEML-F01-D1-DOMAIN).
Physics-derived residual or conservation feature columns required by the candidate, present and unit-labelled (P-NEML-F01-D1-PHYSICS).
Identical frozen split, temporal backbone, seed, horizon, preprocessing provenance, and inherited resource ceiling for baseline and candidate.
Declared held-out predictive target and uncertainty outputs, with calibration and in-distribution/OOD boundaries fixed before comparison.
incompatible_conditions: Non-independent partitions or unresolved trajectory/scenario leakage.
Unavailable labels, target definitions, sampling or horizon metadata, or required physics feature definitions.
Unsupported deployment, control, protection, or operational-use conditions.
Unresolved required inputs or unavailable qualified specialist safety review.

assumptions: The observational unit is an identified transient trajectory/window; the target population is public simulated PWR SB-LOCA data with declared configuration and scenario identities.
Sampling rate, transient horizon, break-extent target, units, and label process are fixed and documented; missingness is measured rather than silently imputed across partitions.
Trajectory and scenario descendants are dependent within an identity and are not treated as independent replicates; exchangeability is assumed only within the frozen declared split.
Stationarity across the evaluated window and class/prevalence balance are not assumed across configurations or scenarios; any shift is reported as a limitation.

Physics-derived residual or conservation features retain declared units; physics constraints are explicit feature or loss terms only where checked, approximate where learned, and unchecked outside the declared preflight.
The baseline and candidate share the frozen split, temporal backbone, seed, horizon, and controls; calibration is evaluated on untouched held-out data.
Generalization across entities, scenarios, sites, time periods, sensors, fidelities, simulator configurations, or plant domains remains a hypothesis until a target-domain decisive test supports it.
baselines: Matched temporal regression on the identical frozen split and resource ceiling.
controls: Use the identical frozen split, temporal backbone, seed, horizon, and inherited resource ceiling for the baseline and candidate.
procedure_outline: Read the manifest, labels, sampling rate, horizon, and partition identities before any fit; stop on a failed precondition.
Only after every preflight passes, fit one matched baseline and one bounded candidate within the inherited ceilings.
Score every bound metric once and record a closed Go, Stop, or Pivot disposition without deployment or safety claims.
Bind C-NEML-F01-D1-PRED to M-NEML-F01-D1-MAE and preconditions P-NEML-F01-D1-MANIFEST, P-NEML-F01-D1-SPLIT, P-NEML-F01-D1-DOMAIN, P-NEML-F01-D1-PHYSICS.
Bind C-NEML-F01-D1-UQ to M-NEML-F01-D1-ECE and the same four route preconditions.
Bind C-NEML-F01-D1-DATA to M-NEML-F01-D1-N and the same four route preconditions.
Derive Go coverage from the route: M-NEML-F01-D1-MAE >= 5.0 percent, M-NEML-F01-D1-ECE <= 0.08 fraction, and M-NEML-F01-D1-N >= 30 count.
Derive Stop coverage from the route: M-NEML-F01-D1-MAE <= -5.0 percent, M-NEML-F01-D1-ECE > 0.15 fraction, and M-NEML-F01-D1-N < 20 count.
Derive Pivot coverage from the route: M-NEML-F01-D1-MAE < 5.0 percent, M-NEML-F01-D1-ECE > 0.08 fraction, and M-NEML-F01-D1-N < 30 count.
uncertainty_handling: Report the uncertainty metric on the untouched held-out split and compare behavior across declared target-domain strata.
Separate sampling, label, measurement, model, optimization, and distribution-shift uncertainty; preserve unstable or unfavorable outcomes.
Do not substitute MAE or trajectory count for ECE, and do not interpret structural validation as uncertainty or safety evidence.
validation_checks: Verify manifest completeness, zero identifier overlap, identical controls, numeric resource logs, and no operational extrapolation.
Confirm route_output is present, selected direction and route traceability match, and approved_constraint_changes is exactly empty before binding the card.
Verify every claim-to-metric and claim-to-precondition mapping is exact, and verify that Go, Stop, and Pivot coverage is present for every bound route metric.
Audit entity, scenario, time, preprocessing, calibration, physics/conservation, sensor-state, and declared OOD separation before interpreting any metric.
Treat structural bundle validation as deterministic offline contract evidence only; it is not model performance, transfer evidence, or nuclear-safety validation.
failure_modes: Trajectory leakage, scenario leakage, simulator shift, class imbalance, horizon mismatch, and calibration-set reuse.
Entity or temporal leakage, preprocessing leakage, label contamination, shortcut learning, or non-independent windows can change the predictive and data claims.
Dataset, simulator, prevalence, configuration, sensor, or target-domain shift can cause miscalibration or OOD overconfidence.
Missing, drifting, biased, saturated, mistimed, or correlated sensor channels can invalidate uncertainty and predictive interpretation.
A learned physics feature or residual can violate dimensional or conservation assumptions; preserve the failure rather than tuning it away.
Exceeding an inherited resource ceiling or bypassing a precondition invalidates the route disposition.
safety_boundaries: Require qualified data, ML, nuclear-domain, VVUQ, instrumentation and controls, human-factors, cybersecurity, privacy, and safety review before any consequential use.
Preserve deterministic protection, interlocks, conservative rules, defense in depth, shutdown authority, and operator authority; the learned component must not replace them.
Keep regulatory, licensing, technical-specification, safety-classification, and facility-procedure decisions outside method coaching and under licensee, regulator, and specialist control.

Do not acquire or upload data, train or run models, download weights, allocate compute, deploy services, issue operational decisions, or claim plant transfer, qualification, licensing, protection, or nuclear-safety success.
